On Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:34 AM hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai wrote:
> I'm attaching a quick draft of an internal egress policy and a replication matrix Rishi and I started.

Thanks — I expanded the matrix and added concrete implementation notes. Summary:

Options (tradeoffs in one line):
- Pattern A — Region-isolated with on-demand rehydration: primary data stored only in EU; indexes/metadata replicated to APAC; rehydration requires explicit customer authorization and a transient key unwrap. Lowest cross-border footprint, higher RTO for full reads.
- Pattern B — Encrypted cross-region replication with per-region CMKs: data replicated to APAC but encrypted with a customer-managed APAC CMK; KMS policies + HSM segregation control key usage. Faster failover, requires cross-region key lifecycle management.
- Pattern C — VPN/Private interconnect replication: keep traffic off the public internet via private peering; still requires clear key separation for compliance.

Operational controls we propose to implement (short list):
- Strict route tables and deny-lists in each private VPC template. Egress only allowed via customer-approved peering endpoints.
- Enforcement hooks in our control plane so that any cross-region copy must be accompanied by a signed policy token (audit log emitted).
- Optional KMS segregation: customer provides per-region KMS keys; Redwood enforces key policy that prevents APAC CMK from accessing EU-only key material.
- Replication job scheduler options: async low-prio (metadata-only) or sync nearline (full object) with audit flags.

Risk notes:
- If SkyBank wants near-instant failover without rehydration, Pattern B is the only reasonable choice, but it implies cross-border storage (albeit encrypted) and more complex key management.
- Metadata-only standbys reduce regulatory exposure but increase application-side complexity and RTO.

I've attached a short doc that can be shared with SkyBank compliance. I included a pointer to INF-1234 where we tracked KMS segregation work.

Jun / team — quick commercial perspective:

- Pattern A (metadata-only standby): feasible on Hosted Private but we should recommend Redwood Dedicated for any service-level guarantees around RTO. Pricing uplift: estimated +18–25% over baseline due to additional orchestration and warm compute.
- Pattern B (per-region CMK replication): requires Dedicated + reserved storage allocation in APAC; will likely need a 12-month commitment for pricing we quoted in the RFP.
- Implementation timeline: PoC with metadata-only standby ~3–4 weeks, full per-region encrypted replication PoC ~8–10 weeks (includes KMS integration and legal signoff).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm whether SkyBank will accept metadata-only standby for initial onboarding.
2) If not, we propose a small-scope PoC of Pattern B limited to a subset of non-sensitive datasets to validate encryption + key rotation workflows.
